rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding nano-ZrC to an HEA bond coat, whereas the paper's intervention is the selection of a specific HVAF spray parameter (medium air/fuel pressure) to optimize deposition of an FeCoNiCrAl coating without any carbide addition.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions high-temperature service with thermal cycling and corrosive exposures, while the paper uses isothermal oxidation in air at 1000–1150 °C for up to 50 h; the temperature range overlaps but the cycling and corrosive atmosphere aspects differ.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a secondary ZrC phase acting as a diffusion barrier, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on low porosity from optimized HVAF spraying and sluggish HEA diffusion to form a protective alumina scale without any secondary phase reinforcement.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced oxidation/corrosion and improved mechanical integrity, while the paper reports controlled alumina TGO growth and no spallation after 50 h; both predict improved oxidation resistance, but the specific property improvements and the underlying cause differ.
